title: Deflated-RankICIR: Multiple-Testing-Aware Factor Selection for LLM-Driven Alpha Mining

contributions.purpose: Corrects multiple testing bias (winner's curse) when selecting factors from large LLM-mined candidate pools ranked by uncorrected validation metrics.
contributions.mechanism: Adapts the Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR) framework from strategy selection to factor-level RankIC time series, creating Deflated-RankICIR, which computes the probability that a factor's observed RankICIR reflects genuine predictive power rather than selection among many trials.
contributions.evaluation: On CSI300 with 70 LLM-mined factors, Deflated-RankICIR achieves the highest Information Ratio (1.717) and best Calmar Ratio (1.456) among all selection methods, outperforming the RankICIR baseline by 3.3%.
contributions.source_quote: We adapt the Deflated Sharpe Ratio framework to factor selection, creating Deflated-RankICIR as a multiple-testing-aware ranking criterion for LLM-driven alpha mining.

contributions.purpose: Identifies why analytical standard error formulas are inadequate for ranking factors under estimation uncertainty.
contributions.mechanism: Uses stationary bootstrap to estimate per-factor standard errors instead of analytical formulas that produce near-constant estimates.
contributions.evaluation: Bootstrap-based estimation creates meaningful rank differentiation (Spearman correlation 0.83 between DSR and RankICIR) whereas analytical formulas fail to distinguish factors.
contributions.source_quote: We identify that bootstrap-based standard error estimation is critical for meaningful rank differentiation, as analytical formulas fail to distinguish factors by estimation uncertainty.

contributions.purpose: Demonstrates that multiple-testing-aware selection improves realized risk-adjusted portfolio returns and that correction strength must be calibrated.
contributions.mechanism: Empirical backtests on CSI300 comparing Deflated-RankICIR against other selection methods, with ablations on the effective-trials interpolation formula including over-correction and no-correction variants.
contributions.evaluation: Deflated-RankICIR improves risk-adjusted returns on CSI300 (IR 1.717, Calmar 1.456); ablations confirm the interpolation formula for effective trials provides optimal correction strength while both over-correction and no correction degrade performance.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate empirically that Deflated-RankICIR improves risk-adjusted returns on CSI300, with the interpolation formula for effective trials providing optimal correction strength.

self_declared_provenance.quote: We address this gap by adapting the Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR) framework (Bailey & de Prado, 2014)—originally designed for strategy selection—to factor-level RankIC time series.
These methods address backtest overfitting at the strategy level but have not been applied to factor selection in alpha mining pipelines.

We bridge the gap between multiple testing correction and factor selection by adapting DSR to RankIC time series. Unlike prior work that applies DSR to strategy-level Sharpe ratios, we compute DSR on factor-level RankICIR, using bootstrap-based standard error estimation to create meaningful rank differentiation among candidates.

notes: Related work contains an explicit 'Our Contribution' paragraph positioning the work as bridging DSR and factor selection. Paper carries a machine-generation warning with code at gitlab.com/fars-a/quantaalpha-multiple-testing-controls.
